comparison.objective: Spike an IV bag and prime its drip chamber without contamination or overfill; candidate uses a locking lifting pin to transfer and fixture a machined part.
comparison.physical_skill: Sterile cap handling, spike insertion, chamber orientation, and controlled squeezing versus close-clearance pin insertion, mechanical locking, shackle lifting, seating, and button-held withdrawal.
comparison.success_condition: Caps removed, spike seated 23–25 mm, liquid level 15–27 mm, uncontaminated and released versus verified retention, 30 mm lift, three-pad support, extracted pin, clearance, and dwell.
comparison.reason: Although both include insertion to a collar, IV priming tests sterility and liquid dosing rather than load-bearing retention and recovery; all versions provide enough thresholds to distinguish them.
